artifacts.summary: Eight-phase implementation plan covering the five extension-manifest quick-fix items, with a findings-baseline gate and per-phase verification tiers.

memory_candidates.content: When a batch of independent config-file fixes shares one file surface (e.g. several extension manifest.json files), phase them one-item-per-phase but serialize any phases touching the SAME file via explicit `Depends on` edges rather than putting them in the same parallel wave. In the extension-manifest batch, two separate defects both edited literature/manifest.json (keyword_overrides shape and the dependencies array) and a third phase swept every manifest for empty stubs; the wave map was built so no two phases in one wave share a file, preserving parallelism for the genuinely independent items while keeping each phase independently revertable. Pair this with a first phase that captures a machine-diffable baseline (verify-deploy.sh --findings) so later phases can prove 'no NEW findings' rather than merely re-asserting 'still passes' -- a subset check against a captured baseline is a strictly stronger gate than an exit-code check, and it is the only way a deploy-footprint-affecting change can be shown not to have perturbed an already-clean tree.
